result.topic_en: Calculations with integer coefficients a_r, b_r, a', b'', c'' and congruences modulo rational numbers (modules), showing that a certain greatest common divisor (module) D equals 1/a and expressing variables w_r, u, v in terms of p, q.
result.transcription:
$\sum\left[b_r - a_r\frac{bb''}{a}\right] + \left[\frac{bb''}{a}\right] = \frac{m}{a}$ ; $m = \sum[ab_r - bb''a_r] + [bb'']$ ; $m$ ganz.
$(ab_r - bb''a_r)a_s - (ab_s - bb''a_s)a_r = a(b_ra_s - a_rb_s) \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{m}{bc}}$
$ab_r - bb''a_r = mc_r$ \quad $b_ra_s - a_rb_s \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{m}{abc}}$
$mc_r\cdot a_s - mc_s\cdot a_r = a(b_ra_s - a_rb_s) \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{m}{bc}}$ ; $b_ra_s - a_rb_s \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{m}{abc}}$
$b'' \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{m}{b}}$, $b'' \equiv 0 \pmod{1}$ ; $[1, \frac{m}{b}] = \frac{1}{p}$ ; $b'' \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{mp}{b}}$
$bcb_r = bc(b_r - a_r\frac{bb''}{a}) + bca_r\cdot\frac{bb''}{a} \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{m}{a}}$ ; $b_r \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{m}{abc}}$
$acb_r - bca_r\cdot b'' \equiv 0 \pmod{mc}$ | $m\sum c_ra'_r = a\frac{b''}{ac} - bb''(\frac{1}{bc} - a') = a'bb''$
Jeder gem. Th. von $b''$, $c$ geht auch | $\sum c_ra'_r = a'\frac{bb''}{m}$
in allen $acb_r$, und natürlich auch
in $ac.1$, also in 1 auf; also $[b'', c] = 1 = a''b'' + cc''$ ; $[a'', c''] = 1$
$acb_r\cdot a'' - bca_r \equiv 0 \pmod{c}$ ; $ac\frac{b''a''}{ac} - bc(\frac{1}{bc} - a') \equiv 0 \pmod{c}$
$a''b'' - 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{c}$.
$a''(ab_r - ba_rb'') = ab_ra'' - ba_r(1 - cc'') = (ab_ra'' - ba_r) + bca_r\cdot c''$
$1 = bca' + \sum bca_r\cdot a'_r$ ; $b'' = \sum acb_r\cdot a'_r$
$cc'' = 1 - a''b'' = bca' + \sum bca_r\cdot a'_r - \sum a''acb_r\cdot a'_r$
$= bca' + \sum(bca_r - acb_ra'')a'_r$
9
$w_r = a_ru + b_rv$ ; $\sum w_ra'_r + a'u = \frac{u}{bc} + \frac{b''v}{ac} = p$ ; $q = \frac{v}{a}$
und $u, v$.
$w_r - bca_rp = (b_r - \frac{bb''a_r}{a})v$ ; $u - bcp = -\frac{bb''v}{a}$ ; $v$ \quad $a_r = a_r$
$\sum[b_r - \frac{bb''}{a}a_r] + [\frac{bb''}{a}] + [1] = \mathfrak{D}$
$b_r - \frac{bb''}{a}a_r = bc\{a'b_r + b_r\sum a_sa'_s\} - bca_r\sum b_sa'_s = bc\{a'b_r + \sum(b_ra_s - a_rb_s)a'_s\} \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{1}{a}}$
$\frac{bb''}{a} \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{1}{a}}$ ; $1 \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{1}{a}}$ ; also $\mathfrak{D} \equiv 0 \pmod{\frac{1}{a}}$
$bc(b_ra_s - a_rb_s) = bca_s(b_r - \frac{bb''}{a}a_r) - bca_r(b_s - \frac{bb''}{a}a_s) \equiv 0 \pmod{\mathfrak{D}}$
$bcb_r = bc(b_r - \frac{bb''}{a}a_r) + bca_r\cdot\frac{bb''}{a} \equiv 0 \pmod{\mathfrak{D}}$
$bca_r$ und $bc \equiv 0 \pmod{1}$, also auch $\equiv 0 \pmod{\mathfrak{D}}$
also $bc\cdot\frac{1}{abc} \equiv 0 \pmod{\mathfrak{D}}$ ; also $\mathfrak{D} = \frac{1}{a}$
Man kann daher $n+2$ ganze Zahlen $h_r$, $h'$, $h''$ so wählen, dass
$\sum(b_r - \frac{bb''}{a}a_r)h_r - h'\frac{bb''}{a} + h'' = \frac{1}{a}$
$\sum(w_r - bca_rp)h_r + (u - bcp)h' + h''v = \frac{v}{a} = q$
$= \sum w_rh_r - bc\sum a_rh_r\cdot p + h'u - bch'p + h''v$
$= \sum w_rh_r - bc\{\sum a_rh_r + h'\}\{\sum w_ra'_r + a'u\} + h'u + h''v$
$w_r = bca_rp + (ab_r - bb''a_r)q$
$u = b(cp - b''q)$
$v = aq$
$p = \sum a'_rw_r + a'u$
$q = \sum b'_rw_r + b'u + c'v$
$p = \sum a'_r\{bca_rp + (ab_r - bb''a_r)q\} + a'b(cp - b''q)$ ; $\sum a_ra'_r + a' = \frac{1}{bc}$ ; $0 = \sum(ab_r - bb''a_r)a'_r - a'bb''$
$q = \sum b'_r\{bca_rp + (ab_r - bb''a_r)q\} + b'b(cp - b''q) + c'aq$ ; $0 = \sum a_rb'_r + b'$ ;
$1 = \sum(ab_r - bb''a_r)b'_r - bb'b'' + c'a = a\sum b_rb'_r + ac'$

Linear substitution expressing w_r,u,v in p,q and inverse
